Modern.brandNameRationale: The crossfader is the slider on a DJ mixer that moves the audio between two decks — the fundamental DJ control. Naming the brand for the control itself puts the act of mixing at the front.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern DJ brands compete on residency, mix series, and label output. There is room for a label-and-residency built around the most foundational mixer control — one name, one slider, a mix series in the middle.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Mixmag (mixmag.net) holds the institutional DJ-media peer. Dekmantel (dekmantel.com) is the considered-modern label-and-festival precedent. Resident Advisor (ra.co) is the global listings reference. We sit closer to Dekmantel in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern label and residency built around the crossfader.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 40. Goes out twice a month. Reads the lineup before the venue. Will travel for a residency.
behaviors: Reads the lineup before the night

dos: Show the lineup and the times

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only — CROSSFADER set in a tight modern grotesk, with a small horizontal slider as the favicon.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and lineups
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for set times and BPM
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the data, the regular carries the brand.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: David Mancuso's invitation-only party The Loft began in 1970 in his Broadway loft — the originating ritual of the New York club tradition that led to Paradise Garage and the modern club. Loft 1970 places the brand in that lineage as a small-membership listening room.
Luxury.industrySummary: Heritage dance-music spaces are rare. There is room for a small-membership listening room in the Loft tradition — invitation-only, a single sound system, no phones, an annual membership fee.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Smalls Jazz Club (smallslive.com) holds the small-membership music-room peer. Brilliant Corners (brilliantcornerslondon.co.uk) is the considered-listening-bar precedent. Spiritland (spiritland.com) is the hi-fi peer. We sit closer to Brilliant Corners in posture, sharper on the membership ritual.
Luxury.positioningStatement: An invitation-only listening room in the Loft tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 40 to 65. Owns a serious sound system. Knows the canon — Mancuso, Levan, Knuckles. Pays an annual membership for the room.
behaviors: Brings a record to the night

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Loft 1970 set in a high-contrast classical serif, with a small woofer-cone pictogram as the hallmark, foiled in brass on the membership card.

typography.primary: Adobe Jenson for the wordmark and invitations
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure member portal
typography.rationale: Jenson carries the heritage register. Söhne handles the member portal.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: A cue point is the marker a digital DJ sets at a specific beat in a track — the place to drop in, the place to loop, the place to fly. Naming the brand for the marker itself puts the precision of the digital DJ at the front.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal DJ brands are uncommon — the category leans maximalist. There is room for a small label and software-adjacent brand whose entire identity is the cue marker — one word, one symbol, one job.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Beatport (beatport.com) holds the institutional-store peer. Bandcamp (bandcamp.com) is the artist-direct precedent. Mixcloud (mixcloud.com) is the mix-platform reference. We sit smaller, sharper on the marker.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimal label organized around the cue point.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. DJs at home and once a month at a friend's bar. Owns a controller and a USB. Buys tracks individually.
behaviors: Buys tracks one at a time
Sets cue points before the night

dos: Publish the BPM and the key
Quote the cue points in the release notes

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only — Cuepoint set in a single-weight grotesk, lowercase. The favicon is a small triangle (the cue-point glyph).

typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for BPM and key data
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the data, the regular carries the brand.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: The long mix is the disco-era extended blend — the twelve-inch single, the ten-minute version, the seamless transition. Naming the operator for the form puts the editorial discipline of the mix at the front.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate-feeling DJ operators run agencies, residency-management firms, and mix-series labels. There is room for an operator built around mix-series curation and residency placement for working DJs.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Defected (defected.com) holds the institutional house-music brand peer. Anjunabeats (anjunabeats.com) plays the agency-and-label precedent. Solid Grooves (solidgrooves.com) sits in the residency middle. We sit smaller, focused on long-form mixes.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A residency-and-mix-series operator for working DJs.

targetAudience.primary: Venue programmers, festival bookers, and brand-event planners booking residencies and long-form mix sets.
behaviors: Manages a roster of touring DJs

dos: Speak to the booker, not the dancer

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a hallmark — The Long Mix set in a clean grotesk, paired with a long horizontal bar as the favicon — the timeline of the mix.

typography.primary: Inter for the wordmark and decks
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed riders and tour books
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across decks. The serif handles the printed rider.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Beatmatching is the foundational DJ skill — adjusting the pitch of one record so its tempo locks with another, the prerequisite for every blend. Naming the club for the skill frames the brand around the craft rather than the night.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative DJ brands lean on visual swagger. There is room for a small workshop-and-night operator built around teaching the craft and running a friendly monthly residency for graduates.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Point Blank Music School (pointblankmusicschool.com) holds the institutional DJ-education peer. Phase One (phaseone.world) is the considered-night precedent. Subtle Radio (subtleradio.com) is the workshop-and-radio peer. We sit closer to Subtle, sharper on the workshop.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative DJ workshop and graduate residency.

targetAudience.primary: 22 to 35. Learning to DJ. Has a controller at home and a USB at the friend's bar. Wants to play out once a month.
behaviors: Plays out at the graduate residency

dos: Photograph the booth, not the dancers

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark with a hand-drawn mark — Beatmatch Club set in a friendly humanist sans, with two small overlapping circles (two records) as the favicon.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and signage
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for workshop dates
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the dates, the regular carries the club.
